name: Jody Thomas
episode: The other side of the cove
life: “I still remember balancing a bottle while perched on a windy bench.” On Sunday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Jody checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I am hoping for a quiet place to feed my baby. I asked the committee to bring their measuring tape at high tide.
appearance: Jody has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Jody raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Jody never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Jody can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To test the bench at high tide while holding a baby.
family: Ada Ellis is Jody’s cousin raised in the same household. Jody brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Ada makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The sheltered corner*, Ada says, “I gave directions using the old stop. A stranger arrived late for a reunion and I want to write to the host.”
connections: Adela Marin. Testing a seat with a baby on one knee shows the bolt supplier what the finished dimensions mean.

reactions.response: Jody asks the cleaner and the donor for separate views on the wording.

reactions.response: Jody suggests one straightforward message without accusations and gives the friend time to answer.
